entries.origin_analysis: Family G tested whether a single return inside the original breakout level was a structural invalidation signal.
entries.causal_hypothesis: A single structural return identifies permanent F05 failure.
pre_result_predictions: one cell is positive in all three development periods
falsified_or_unsupported_claims: single-checkpoint structural return separates permanent failure from recovery winners
retained_findings: the trigger removes losses but sacrifices similar winner value
prohibited_reuse: do not expand Family G thresholds

entries.origin_analysis: Persistent no-reacceptance populations were negative in all three development periods, motivating a fixed two-checkpoint exit family.
entries.causal_hypothesis: Persistent structural invalidation without reacceptance identifies permanent F05 failure more reliably than one checkpoint.
pre_result_predictions: one frozen cell produces positive net and PF at least 1 in every period
entries.decision: Close Family H before MT4 parity or 2025 access.
falsified_or_unsupported_claims: two-checkpoint non-reacceptance is a robust fixed early-exit rule
negative subgroup baseline P/L implies positive replacement-exit value
retained_findings: late recovery after the second checkpoint remains the decisive winner-sacrifice source
delayed checkpoints did not determine the result
prohibited_reuse: do not expand Family H checkpoints or thresholds
do not add shadow strategy health
successor_questions: which trajectory feature available by the second checkpoint predicts late recovery?

entries.origin_analysis: Family H improved some 2023 trades but harmed both 2024 halves because positions that remained invalidated through 60 or 90 minutes could still recover later.
entries.causal_hypothesis: No candidate hypothesis is active. Diagnose trajectory features observable by the second checkpoint that distinguish late recovery from permanent failure.
pre_result_predictions: recovery winners and permanent failures differ in at least one no-lookahead trajectory feature across all three periods
the feature is distinct from closed Families D-H
entries.decision: Remain descriptive until duplicate-research and novelty audit supports a finite successor family.
retained_findings: single and persistent invalidation are insufficient
the unresolved gap is late recovery capacity after the second checkpoint
prohibited_reuse: do not use 2025 for feature selection
do not infer exit value from subgroup baseline loss
successor_questions: does recovery velocity, rebound quality or checkpoint-to-checkpoint trajectory separate the populations?
